title: Declarative EKS control-plane bootstrapper with preflight sentinels and self-heal policies
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: ship a reusable Terraform module and orchestration shim that performs declarative bootstrapping of the Redwood Private EKS control plane with preflight sentinels, automated remedial actions, clear observability hooks, and documented rollback paths. The module should be idempotent, safe for repeated apply in multi-account setups, and provide safety gates for upgrades (schema and k8s API compatibility checks).

Background: we continue to see upgrade-induced regressions in private EKS clusters during control-plane upgrades and initial bootstrapping. Current provisioners are fragile when IAM, KMS, or cross-account role constraints change mid-run. This ticket builds a safety-first layer: a preflight validation phase, a bootstrap executor that records intent, and a small runtime (stateless) controller used during provisioning to perform retries and self-heal common transient failures.

Acceptance criteria:
- Terraform module (module.tgz) that creates EKS control plane resources and related IAM/KMS hooks with a single entrypoint variable set for "declarative_state" and idempotent behavior.
- Preflight sentinel checks executed as a separate terraform plan/apply step that produce explicit failure reasons for IAM/KMS/networking/cni/amzn-eks-managed-policy mismatches.
- A bootstrap orchestrator (lightweight container image + helm chart) deployed optionally to a management cluster which watches bootstrap runs and executes three remedial strategies: retry with exponential backoff, rollback partial resources, and mark manual-intervention-required with diagnostics.
- Health checks: post-bootstrap probes for endpoint reachability, control-plane node readiness, RBAC sanity, and KMS access patterns; results emitted to CloudWatch/Datadog with tags: env, cluster, bootstrap_run_id.
- Documented canary and upgrade flow with explicit preflight steps to run before every control-plane upgrade.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- We keep the orchestrator minimal (stateless) to avoid increasing support burden; state is stored in a namespaced S3 key (or k8s configmap as fallback) so multiple bootstrap runs are observable and resumable. Chose S3 for cross-account resilience.
- Using Terraform-driven preflight separate from main apply reduces blast radius but requires an additional CI step; trade is acceptable for higher safety on customer clusters.
- Rollback is best-effort: we will implement targeted cleanup handlers (eg. delete CRDs created by bootstrap) rather than full transactional rollback of all cloud resources. Documented limitations clearly in README.

Implementation plan:
1) Prototype preflight module and checks (IAM policies, VPC subnets, route table associations, required service-linked roles).
2) Build Terraform module with explicit outputs (bootstrap_run_id, manifest_bucket, sentinel_report_url).
3) Publish bootstrapper container image and helm chart to internal registry.
4) Wire observability: CloudWatch metrics + Datadog integration plus a simple dashboard template.
5) Run 3 staged canaries: internal dev cluster, partner test cluster, and one customer pilot.

Security and compliance notes:
- All KMS accesses are audited; module supports customer KMS keys and cross-account grants.
- Secrets never stored in plaintext: bootstrapper uses IAM role with session credentials.
- Security review flagged: cross-account S3 access pattern in step 2 requires design doc and SRE sign-off (see links).

Testing and rollout:
- Unit tests for terraform module with terratest.
- End-to-end CI flow that runs preflight -> terraform apply with ephemeral org-lab account.
- Post-apply health probe suite run as part of CI, failing the pipeline on critical probes.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/priv-eks/bootstrap-safetykit
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules/pull/412
- Helm chart: https://github.com/redwood-inference/charts/tree/main/eks-bootstrapper

Risks and mitigation:
- Risk: cross-account KMS/S3 grants lead to slow permission debugging. Mitigation: provide an automated IAM diff in preflight that shows exact policy changes and pre-signed test objects.
- Risk: added complexity causes longer onboarding. Mitigation: include an "opinionated quickstart" with minimal flags that works in 90% of internal setups.

Next steps:
- Finish terratest harness and add Datadog dashboard JSON by 2026-03-12.
- Create initial customer pilot plan and run with support engineers by 2026-03-22.

Notes: this ticket intentionally scopes the module and lightweight runtime together so operators have a clear remediation path during the fragile bootstrap period. If the runtime proves problematic we will split it into a separate optional repo and revert to runbook-only coverage.
